rebuttal_or_critique: While I acknowledge the concerns regarding food inflation at 8.52%, it remains primarily a supply-side phenomenon that is less responsive to interest rate hikes. With core inflation at 3.25%, the real policy rate is already sufficiently restrictive to anchor expectations. Maintaining a stance of 'withdrawal of accommodation' when the output gap is only +0.40% risks overtightening and unnecessarily constraining the 6.30% GVA growth momentum. A shift to 'neutral' better reflects the current macroeconomic reality where the policy rate is already at an appropriate level to guide inflation toward the 4.00% target without imposing an excessive growth sacrifice.
